metaDescription: Big Piney sits at the heart of the Jonah Field, one of the most drilled tight-gas plays in Wyoming. Get a real read on your Sublette County mineral interest.
heroLead: Big Piney sits inside the Jonah Field, one of the densest tight-gas developments anywhere in the Rockies, and mineral interests here carry more actual production history than almost anywhere else on my list.
intro: The Jonah Field, developed since the late 1990s targeting the Lance Formation, has been drilled on unusually tight spacing compared to older Wyoming fields, which means a lot of Sublette County mineral owners around Big Piney have real, ongoing royalty statements rather than speculative acreage. Operators here have included Jonah Energy and predecessors through several rounds of ownership changes over the years.

If you're holding a mineral interest in this area, there's a strong chance it's tied to an active or recently active well, and I want your actual royalty history in hand before I quote anything, because that data tells the real story better than county averages ever could.

sections.heading: Jonah Field development
paragraphs: The Lance Formation here is a classic tight-gas reservoir, requiring dense well spacing to drain effectively, which is why Jonah has one of the highest well counts per section of any Wyoming field. That density is good news for mineral owners inside the unit boundary, since it usually means multiple wells contributing to a single royalty interest rather than one.

Decline curves on tight-gas wells drop faster than conventional oil in the early years, then flatten into a long, low tail. Where your specific wells sit on that curve matters enormously to what your interest is worth today.

sections.heading: Pricing an active Jonah interest
paragraphs: I start with your trailing twelve months of royalty statements to establish current cash flow, then adjust for where the underlying wells sit on their decline curve and what commodity price assumptions are reasonable right now. Natural gas pricing swings hard, so any number I give reflects current activity, hedged against near-term volatility, not a fixed promise.

sections.heading: Ownership near Sublette County's boom towns
paragraphs: Big Piney and neighboring Marbleton grew fast during the Jonah and Pinedale development years, and a lot of mineral interests here changed hands, split among heirs, or got partially sold off during that period. I check the Sublette County recorder's full chain of title before quoting, since partial prior sales are common in this area.

faqs.question: Is Jonah Field still being actively drilled?
faqs.answer: Development has slowed from its peak years, but the field continues to produce and see periodic infill activity. I'll check your specific unit's current status.

faqs.question: My royalty checks have dropped significantly. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Tight-gas wells decline steeply after initial production, then level off. A drop doesn't necessarily mean the well is done, but it does affect current value.

faqs.question: How is natural gas pricing handled in your offer?
faqs.answer: I peg any number to current market activity and your actual recent statements, not a fixed assumption about future gas prices.
